parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
The rear wheel and the pedals of a bicycle are connected by a chain that passes around two cogs (toothed wheels), as shown in Fig. 1.1.

[[fig:f1]]

The small cog has a radius of 0.038 m and is fixed to the rear wheel so that it rotates with it. The large cog has a radius of 0.15 m and is fixed to the pedals so that it rotates with them. The rear wheel has a radius of 0.46 m.

The bicycle is being pedaled so that it moves in a straight line at a constant speed of 17 m s⁻¹.
parts.text: Calculate the angular speed of the rear wheel.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the period of rotation of the small cog.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Show that the distance moved by point X on the chain during one full rotation of the small cog is 0.24 m.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text: Use the information in (b)(iii) to determine the angle through which the large cog rotates during one full rotation of the small cog.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The chain of the bicycle in (b) is moved onto a smaller cog fixed to the rear wheel. The speed of the bicycle does not change.

Explain, without calculation, the effect of this change on the angular speed of the pedals.

figures.caption: Fig. 1.1 (not to scale)
figures.alt: A bicycle chain passes around small and large cogs, with the rear wheel, pedals, and point X labelled.
